strengths: Strong empirical speedups (15.63× on LLaDA, 34.22× with caching) on important practical problem
Comprehensive evaluation across 8 benchmarks and 2 models with thorough ablation studies
Clear motivation with concrete empirical observations (Figure 1) of token confidence convergence and positional clustering
Well-written paper with effective visualizations and clear presentation of methodology
Demonstrated compatibility with existing optimization techniques (dLLM-Cache) and competitive throughput vs. autoregressive baselines (LLaMA3 8B)
Reasonable accuracy preservation in most cases, with some tasks showing improvements (MMLU +4.45%)
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: the three 'golden principles' are standard ML observations (confidence reliability, convergence in iterative refinement, spatial clustering) with minimal theoretical justification or analysis

Unjustified technical design choices: variance-based stability criterion (Eq. 8) lacks principled justification; simple endpoint prediction (Eq. 7) is overly simplistic; no analysis of why these specific formulations are optimal
Method complexity with 5+ hyperparameters lacking generalization guidance; unclear how to set hyperparameters for new models/domains without task-specific tuning

Incomplete experimental analysis: no evaluation on sequences >1024 tokens, missing task-specific breakdown of where method succeeds/fails, no standard deviations reported, undefined baselines (e.g., 'Diffusion Sampling' in Table 3)
Non-trivial accuracy drops on some tasks (Math -0.52%, BBH -0.37%) become larger with caching (Math -0.74%, MBPP -1.80%), contradicting 'minimal accuracy drop' claim

Reproducibility concerns: no code link provided despite mention in abstract, missing model version details, dependent on concurrent work (dLLM-Cache), generalization to other dLLM architectures and hardware unclear
Missing ablations isolating component contributions and analysis of computational overhead of the stability check mechanism itself

strengths: Clear articulation of three empirically-grounded principles (Certainty, Convergence, Positional) that effectively guide the sampling strategy design, supported by good visualization and intuition

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 benchmarks and 2 dLLM architectures with strong results: up to 15.63× speedup alone and 34.22× with caching, demonstrating dLLMs can match/exceed autoregressive LLM throughput
Thorough ablation studies examining key hyperparameters (τmin_conf, τhigh_conf, Kmax, Whist, σ²stable) with clear sensitivity analysis and well-motivated default values
Well-designed two-stage pipeline that is technically sound with clear mathematical formulations and good engineering integration with existing dLLM-Cache mechanisms
Maintains comparable accuracy while achieving substantial speedups in most cases (minimal degradation <1% on many benchmarks), providing good speed-quality trade-offs
weaknesses: Core novelty is limited—the three principles are relatively straightforward empirical observations, and the technical contribution primarily applies these to engineer a practical system rather than introducing novel methodological insights

Method introduces 7+ hyperparameters requiring tuning (τmin_conf, τhigh_conf, Kmax, Whist, σ²stable, kslow, kfast); lacks principled guidance for hyperparameter selection on new models/tasks without validation data

Some accuracy-speed trade-offs are non-trivial (e.g., GPQA: -2.68% at 34.22× speedup); paper underexplores analysis of accuracy degradation patterns and does not provide guidance for choosing hyperparameters based on desired accuracy targets

Several technical design choices lack strong justification: Why is variance of convergence horizon the right stability metric? Why is the simple max operation optimal for End Point prediction (Eq. 7)? 'Aggressive unmasking' vaguely specified
Experimental evaluation limited to single GPU (RTX 4090); no multi-GPU scaling, statistical significance testing, or error bars; some baseline comparisons (semi-autoregressive) appear underdeveloped

Incomplete analysis of failure modes and edge cases; no discussion of sequence length sensitivity, very short sequences, or guidance on when NOT to use the method; how does exploratory stage length vary by task?

Figure 3 is dense and difficult to parse; notation inconsistencies across indices; title 'Three Golden Principles' feels somewhat marketing-oriented; limited discussion of related speculative decoding and parallel inference methods

Stability check design appears ad-hoc and empirically optimized without theoretical justification; Whist=2 seems very small and no analysis provided of how often stability criterion is met or typical exploratory stage lengths

strengths: Substantial and impressive speedups (15-34×) with practical significance; LLaDA with SlowFast+Cache outperforms LLaMA3 8B in throughput while maintaining competitive accuracy
Comprehensive evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks and 2 dLLM models with multiple baselines and thorough ablation studies
Excellent reproducibility with detailed algorithm specification, hyperparameter configurations, case studies, and promised code release
Demonstrates clean composability with existing acceleration methods (dLLM-Cache), showing orthogonal improvements
Well-executed experimental work with clear presentation and effective visualizations of the confidence dynamics
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: confidence-based sampling, convergence detection, and positional clustering are known techniques; the core contribution is their algorithmic combination rather than fundamental innovation

Overclaiming about accuracy: Tables 1-2 show notable accuracy drops on several tasks (Dream -1.23% to -3.20%, LLaDA up to -0.52%), contradicting claims of 'lossless acceleration' and 'minimal accuracy drop'

High hyperparameter complexity with 7 key parameters requiring tuning; methodology for hyperparameter selection (τmin_conf=0.1, τhigh_conf=0.85) not clearly explained; transferability to new models unclear
Limited generalization: only 2 dLLM models tested (both 2025 models); no evidence the method generalizes to other dLLM architectures; unclear if results persist as the emerging dLLM field matures

Weak theoretical foundation: stability check using variance is ad-hoc with no justification for this choice; no theoretical analysis of why principles should work; connection between confidence convergence and correct decoding assumed rather than proven

Positional Principle underspecified and least well-motivated; could result from other factors (prompt bias, local context); non-contiguous block handling seems to require additional mechanisms not fully explained

Incomplete analysis: no investigation of failure modes; unexplained variance in benchmark speedups (GSM8K 3.2× vs BBH 5.24×); Figure 1(b) confidence map intriguing but underanalyzed; missing memory/latency analysis
Missing comparisons: limited baselines beyond Fast-dLLM; no statistical significance testing; no comparison with other acceleration approaches (distillation, quantization, speculative decoding)
